title: CreatorBrief
description: The nine pre-spend decisions for one video run — Block C of the video brief template, keyed to a plan item and written to content/<active>/video/<script-slug>/brief.json BEFORE anything is generated. It is NOT the plan item's own `brief` field (that is what to say; this is how to make it) and it is NOT an approval step: the brief is produced under the existing Gate 1 envelope and there is no `brief` gate kind.

item_id.description: ContentItem.id this brief governs, or a minted id for an ad-hoc piece. A field inside the brief, never part of its path — the path is the run folder.

script_slug.description: <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>, the run folder's name under content/<active>/video/. Mints the folder this brief is the first artifact of.

written_on.description: ISO-8601 date the brief was written.

profile.description: Active profile slug this brief is bound to.

product.description: Product slug, when the run is product-scoped.

decisions.description: All nine are required. A brief missing one is refused at WRITE time rather than read time — a half-written brief that downstream skills read as complete is the failure this refusal exists for.

cover.$comment: decision 1 — the cover is designed BEFORE the content and binds framing, palette and headline.

source.description: Per-field provenance, inherited whole from the 2026-08-28 video brief template. A decision with a default is filled and labelled, never asked; the operator is asked only for a decision with no default. A brief that is complete because every field defaulted is legal and SAYS SO — that is what stops an all-default brief from reading as if someone decided.

outlier_structure.$comment: decision 2 — mine 3-5 outliers, extract the STRUCTURE, never the content.

name.description: The named structure, committed to. A description is not a name.

beats.description: Beat order only. Lifting an outlier's CONTENT is prohibited.

A story item (one whose plan item carries brief.protagonist) derives live_action with source=derived and the preflight's reason, per gtm_core.video_preflight.story_capture — filled and labelled, never asked.

criterion.description: How the winner is picked. Declared and recorded per render — a best-of-N with no declared criterion is refused rather than defaulting to 'first'.

visual_hook.$comment: decision 9 — the first frame as a SHOT SPEC, not a vibe. Distinct from the cover: same subject, different job.

expression.description: The face in the first frame, written as muscles at a stated size: one region moving and how far, what holds still, and where the eyes go. An adjective ('amused', 'confident') names a category and not a size, so the render resolves the size from stock imagery and returns a reaction shot. Grammar and the per-beat registers: creator-brief/references/performance-lexicon.md. This is the hook frame only — every later beat carries its own expression on the shot list, where the refused vocabulary and the region ceiling are enforced.

recognisable_element.description: The familiar thing beside the novel one — recognition before beauty.

caption_voice.$comment: decision 10 (optional) — sets the narrative caption mode, voice, cross-beat threads, and anchor beats.

mode.description: subtitles = speech-anchored transcription; narrative = thought-anchored storytelling alongside picture.

voice.description: Who is speaking (e.g. 'close narrator', 'inner voice', 'second person', 'character', 'choric').

thread.description: Motif word/phrase pairs connecting shots across the film.

anchor_beats.description: Shot numbers where anchorage (literal narrowing of image meaning) is intentionally used (e.g. premise or message beats).

$comment: The provenance enum is INLINED on all nine decisions rather than shared through $defs: gtm_core.minischema — the validator this schema actually runs through — ignores $ref entirely, so a shared definition would read as enforced and enforce nothing. Same reason shots.schema.json declines maxItems.
